explanations.23: json.dumps() converts the Python dictionary into a JSON string, then .encode() converts that string into bytes so it can be sent over the network.
explanations.32: This calculates the dot product—multiply each pair of corresponding numbers from vectors a and b, then add them all up.
explanations.33: The denominator computes the magnitude (length) of each vector by squaring all elements, summing them, and taking the square root; dividing by both magnitudes gives us the cosine similarity, a score from -1 to 1 showing how similar two vectors are.
explanations.36: sys.argv[1:] grabs command-line arguments after the script name; the 'or' part provides a default model name if no arguments were passed.
explanations.41: The angle brackets and numbers like '<20' and '<5' are format specifiers that pad the text to a certain width, making the output columns line up nicely.
